segments: The Chronography of Bar Hebraeus.
16, died, having lived {OCR?} four years.
A rebellion arose against him by a certain brave man {OCR?} from al-Hira,
whose name was likewise Yazid ibn al-Muhallab.
And all the Arabs of 'Aqula (Kufa), and of Basra, and of all Persia were with him.
And Yazid ibn 'Abd al-Malik sent against him a large army,
and Yazid ibn al-Muhallab was defeated near Babylon and was killed.
And Yazid commanded,
and the images of every living thing were wiped out
from temples, and from walls, and wood, and from stones, and from books.
And Leo, the emperor of the Romans, also did likewise,
and he took down the icons of the saints and of the emperors from churches and houses.
And for this reason, there was an uprising among the Romans,
and many openly murmured against the emperor.
He also expelled from his territory anyone who did not submit to the Council of Chalcedon.
And he pressured the Jews,
and many of them were baptized,
while the rest fled to Syria.
And at this time, a certain Syrian man whose name was Severus claimed of himself that he was the Messiah.
And when he was arrested by the governor, he said:
"I was mocking the Jews."
And in the year 1032,
(1032 of the Greeks,
721 of our Lord?), the waters of the springs dried up,
so that the villagers had to go seven miles to draw water;
and there was a shortage of crops.
And after a year, a great swarm of locusts came
and destroyed the crops.
And after two years, there was a pestilence caused by the disease of dysentery {OCR?},
and especially in Mesopotamia.
And in the year 1037,
[after Yazid, reigned his brother] {OCR?} Hisham ibn 'Abd al-Malik for twelve years and eight months.
This man oppressed
the people with excessive levies and tributes.
And he dug canals from the Euphrates above Callinicus for the irrigation of crops and plantations,
and the revenue from them exceeded all the tribute of his realm.
And in that same year, the Arabs fell upon Neo-Caesarea of Pontus,
and completely destroyed it.
And the Arabs also passed into the land of the Turks with Jarrah {OCR?} the general,
and conquered a large city,
and took great spoil and departed.
And in the year 1038,
(1038 of the Greeks?), the Egyptians rebelled against the Arabs,
